what_it_measured.text: Scalable Purification and Characterization of the Anticancer Lunasin Peptide from Soybean

dose.text: In vitro binding of synthetic and purified lunasin (0.1, 1, 10 and 100 μM) to human recombinant core histones H3 and H4 was assessed utilizing a modified ELISA format using 500 ng of either H3 or H4 as the capture protein.

endpoint.text: In vitro binding of synthetic and purified lunasin (0.1, 1, 10 and 100 μM) to human recombinant core histones H3 and H4 was assessed utilizing a modified ELISA format using 500 ng of either H3 or H4 as the capture protein.

reported_results.text: Varying the ratio of extraction solution volume to amount of white flake over a range of 5:1 to 12.5:1 (buffer:white flake) also did not have a significant effect on the amount of lunasin recovered.

White flake was mixed with extraction buffer (75.5 mM sodium phosphate, 68.4 mM NaCl, 10 mM sodium metabisulfite, 20 mM ascorbic acid, pH 7.4) at a 12.5:1 buffer to biomass ratio and mixed for one hour at 4°C.
These results also indicated that all cysteine residues in the lunasin complex are involved in disulfide bonds and that there are 2 disulfide bonds between lunasin and the 8975.1 Da subunit.

ESI-MS analysis of the lunasin complex after reduction with DTT and alkylation with IAA demonstrated that the 5141.3 Da and 8975.1 Da complex subunits contain two and six cysteine residues, respectively (Figure 7A).
Upon reduction of the complex with DTT, the most abundant isotopic masses corresponding to the two subunits of the complex were 5141.3 Da and 8975.1 Da Figure 7A).
